chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: When a child of a believer dies,
and Allah is most Knowing of what the servant said,
Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says to His angels: 'Did you take the child of so-and-so?'
So He says: 'So what did My servant say?'
They say: 'He praised You and said Istirja (returned to Allah).'
So Allah, Blessed and Exalted, says: 'You took the fruit of his heart and the delight of his eyes,'
'and he praised Me and said Istirja.'
'Build for him a house in Paradise and name it the House of Praise.'

key_terms.اسْتَرْجَعَ: Said Istirja (recited 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un')
key_terms.بَيْتَ الْحَمْدِ: House of Praise (a specific dwelling in Paradise)
key_terms.ثَمَرَةَ قَلْبِهِ: Fruit of his heart (metaphor for a beloved child)
key_terms.قُبِضَ: Taken (referring to the soul being taken by angels)
key_terms.قُرَّةَ عَيْنِهِ: Delight of his eyes (metaphor for joy/comfort)

ai.seo_question: What reward does Allah promise for a believer who patiently praises Him when their child dies?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates that when a believer's child dies, Allah inquires about the parent's response to the angels' report of the soul's taking. Upon confirming the parent said 'Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un' (Istirja), Allah rewards their patience by commanding the construction of a specific dwelling in Paradise called 'Bayt al-Hamd' (The House of Praise), highlighting the spiritual merit of gratitude during bereavement.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘When a child of a believer dies, and Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is more Knowing with what the servant says (during the bereavement), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Says to His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels: “Did you capture a child of so and so?”
So they are saying: ‘Yes, our Lord<sup>azwj</sup>!’
So He<sup>azwj</sup> is Saying: “So what did My<sup>azwj</sup> servant say?”
They are saying: ‘He praised Youazwj and said [2:156] Surely we are for Allah and to Him we are returning’.
So Allahazwj Blessed and High is Saying: “You took the fruit of his heart and the delight of his eyes and he praised Meazwj and said [2:156] Surely we are for Allah and to Him we are returning.
Build a house for him in the Paradise and name it as the House of Praise’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘
When a son of a believing person dies
- Allah knows what the servant (of Allah) may say -
Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, says to His angels, “Have you taken the soul of the son of My servant out of his body?”
They reply, “Yes, O Lord, we have done so.”
He then asks, “What did My servant say?”
They say, “He praised You and said, ‘We are for Allah and to Him we return.’”
Allah, the Most Holy, the Most High, then says, “So you took away the fruit of his heart and the delight of his eyes
but he praised Me and spoke of his return to Me.
(For his reward) build a house for him in paradise and call it the house of al-Hamd (praising Allah).””’
